title: The journey and the choice
goal: Explain why the boy chose the school and map his journey.
reading: The Same Way · story and questions
reading_task: Read the whole story once for meaning. Revisit the opening and journey. Find the reason for choosing this school and put the five travel stages in order. Use selected sentence slides only where help is needed.
grammar: Part A · possession and location, slides 4–36
grammar_task: Use slides 5, 10 and 21, then one example per rule. Complete Part A tasks 1–2. Keep early answers for comparison. Remaining examples are home practice.
writing_task: Write two sentences about the journey and one about what the boy has. In the final four minutes, explain the difference between He has and There is.
prep: Bring the story worksheet, Part A sheet and notebook.
Think about how you get to school.
home: Reread the journey with audio. Retell the route in order.
../follow-along/
Review Part A slides 4–36 and correct one sentence without erasing your first attempt.
../there-is-there-are/#4
Finish story questions 1–2 and write one new There is sentence.
../the-same-way/files/the-same-way-worksheet.pdf
check: Accept a correct route and a text-based reason. Check possession and location separately.
support: Let pupils point to evidence and say their answer before writing.
exit: Explain the school choice using a detail from the story.

title: Rain, friends and questions
skills: Explain a change in the story
goal: Explain what changes when the boy meets his classmates and what remains uncertain.
reading: The Same Way · rain and classroom ending
reading_task: Revisit the rain worry and the classroom ending. Find evidence that the boy did not know the other boys were his classmates. Discuss shared feelings. Complete questions 3–6, including the unresolved rain problem.
grammar: Part A · negatives and questions, slides 37–81
grammar_task: Model with slides 37 and 58, then one example each. Use worksheet tasks 3–4 and collect the sheet before showing the answer slides. Revisit errors next meeting.
writing_task: Write one negative and one question about a room. Answer one story question with evidence. In the final four minutes, explain why finding friends does not solve the rain problem.
prep: Bring your story answers and Part A sheet.
Prepare one detail that shows the boy’s feelings.
home: Replay the ending and retell what changes in the classroom.
../follow-along/
Review selected negative and question examples in slides 37–80.
../there-is-there-are/#37
Finish story questions 3–6 and improve one answer with evidence.
../the-same-way/files/the-same-way-worksheet.pdf
check: Do not accept that he knew they were classmates or that the rain problem is solved.
support: Separate the practical problem from the change in feelings. Rehearse a question aloud.
exit: Write an Is there or Are there question without copying.

title: Reading workshop: a message and information

goal: Use evidence to answer questions about two short texts.
reading: Feedback slides · open after independent work
reading_task: Use the printed sheet first: 9 minutes for the message and tasks 1–3, 11 for the information text and tasks 5–8, then 4 for paired evidence checking. Keep feedback slides closed until pupils have tried.

title: Transfer, question words and exam practice
skills: Apply reading skills to a new message
Write and check a short message independently
goal: Apply the unit skills independently before the first exam on 22 October.
reading: First exam preparation · question words and How
reading_task: Allow 6 minutes for tasks 9–10 independently and collect before answers. Use 12 minutes for selected question-word and How examples, then 6 to justify answers with evidence. Sample the deck rather than running every slide.
grammar_task: Use the collected work to revisit there is/are and have/has, one negative and one question. Pupils answer first, then check. Past forms in Part B are an extension after this exam.
writing_task: Write a new three-sentence school message without a model. Check meaning first, then one grammar point. Use the last four minutes to name one skill to practise before the exam.
prep: Bring both worksheets and your revised message.
Choose one question you still have about the unit.
home: Review the story and retell the choice, worry and ending.
../follow-along/
Practise selected question-word and How questions.
../first-exam-preparation/
Review the workshop and write a fresh short message, then check it.
reading/?mode=home
check: Use the new-message answers to check transfer. Judge meaning before spelling.
support: Give a brief planning prompt, then let pupils write independently.
exit: Identify one personal review target for 22 October.
